source.note: The reproduction artifact's caps live in the Node bundler, which the Godot runtime cannot import. This file is the res://-readable view of them, not a second authority. tests/repro-budget.test.mjs asserts these values equal the exported constants, so the two cannot drift.

measured.note: Measured rather than estimated. The event cap alone suggested roughly 40 grenades; the byte cap binds first and the real figure is about 18. Do not restate the event-cap number.

warn_note: Option E from OBSERVATION-001: the worst property of this limit is its silence. Warning at three quarters of the binding cap puts the information in front of the player while a mission can still be ended cleanly, rather than after the artifact has already failed closed.
baseline_note: Everything the finished artifact carries beyond the replay bundle the runtime can measure: identity, manifest, SHA256SUMS, mechanical and artifact digests. Subtracted from the byte cap so the readout reaches 100% where the artifact actually fails. NOT guessed -- calibrated against the measured exhaustion point. A live ledger costs 227.3 bytes per terrain event, and OBSERVATION-001 measured the byte cap exhausted at 462 terrain events, so 128000 - (462 * 227.3) = 23136, pinned at 23000. The first attempt at this used a guessed 9000, which made the readout report 88% at the point the artifact was already full -- an optimistic readout on a feature whose entire purpose is honesty about a limit. Re-derive this the same way if the artifact envelope changes. Still an approximation: the bundler remains the gate and still fails closed.
